sections.h2: Before you sell a Sebastian house fast
sections.html:
Picking among a realtor, a private sale and a cash buyer starts with two questions: when do you need to close, and what does the house need? Sebastian sits on the Indian River Lagoon in Indian River County, and the population is about 27,352. Roughly 85.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and a typical owner-estimated home value is $317,000, so compare recent nearby sales before you pick a price.

Most of the work is paperwork. The clerk records deeds, the tax collector bills each parcel, and the building department keeps permit files. Knowing who holds what saves days.

  • Request the permit history from the city's building department.
  • Find out whether a homestead exemption sits on the parcel.
  • Keep the deed, any survey and recent repair invoices in one folder.

sections.h2: Older homes in a slow-moving market
sections.html:
About 89 percent of residents live at the same address a year later, so homes change hands slowly. Houses held for decades often still have older finishes and older permit files, and buyers will look for both.

Much of the city was platted from a 1957 purchase of 1,345 acres by a Miami developer to start Sebastian Highlands. Houses from that era may be due for a new roof, air handler or water heater, which is why many owners here look at cash offers.

sections.h2: Permits that can slow a sale
sections.html:
Open or expired permits are the most common snag. Check with the city building department at 1225 Main St., phone 772-589-5537. Applications go through the MGO portal or by email, with uploads capped at 30MB.

An owner-builder can use the portal, but the first application must be made in person, a rule the city ties to Florida law. Inspections are booked through the portal at least one day ahead. The city offers free video inspections for air conditioning replacement, electrical panel change-outs and plumbing water heater or re-pipe work, which helps when nobody is home to let the inspector in.

  • Ask whether any permit on your address is still open.
  • If a roof, air conditioner or water heater was replaced, find the permit and final inspection.
  • If work was done without a permit, tell the buyer or buyer's agent up front, not at the inspection.

Cash buyers will usually take a house with unpermitted work and price it in. Closing out permits first can raise what a conventional buyer will pay.

sections.h2: Property taxes at a Sebastian closing
sections.html:
The Indian River County property appraiser values each parcel as of January 1, and bills go out in November. When the house transfers, a capped assessment resets to just value, so a long-time owner's low bill rarely follows the house. August brings the notice of proposed taxes.

Paying early earns a printed discount of 4 percent in November, dropping a point each month to 1 percent in February. At a late-year closing, your title agent splits the bill by days of ownership.

The exemption removes up to $50,000 of taxable value, though only the first $25,000 counts for school taxes. You apply by March 1 and must live in the house permanently as of January 1. Renting it out ends the exemption.

The exemption follows the owner, not the house, so your buyer files their own application. Call the county property appraiser to learn what your parcel carries.

sections.h2: Recording fees and stamp tax on the deed
sections.html:
Typical charges on a Sebastian deed
ChargeAmountWho sets it
Documentary stamp tax70 cents per $100 of priceState of Florida
Recording, first page$5Clerk, under s. 28.24
Recording, each added page$4Clerk, under s. 28.24

The clerk adds trust fund and technology fees on top. Stamp tax is collected at recording and grows with price and assumed debt. The Department of Revenue holds each signer liable, but your contract decides who pays. Payoffs for mortgages, liens and unpaid taxes come out of proceeds, and title charges vary by company.

Ask for the buyer's cost split in writing.

sections.h2: Who chooses a cash sale in Sebastian?
sections.html:
Cash suits owners who value speed or condition over top price. With so many homeowners and a large share of residents over 65, typical sellers here include heirs, owners moving into assisted living and people who would rather not replace an aging roof or air handler.

Compare net proceeds, not headline numbers. A listing can bring more but adds showings, post-inspection repair requests and a longer wait. A cash buyer may pay less and still close sooner. Ask each one for the closing date, who pays title and recording costs, and whether the offer survives their own inspection. Get each answer in writing before you sign.

Start by confirming who has authority to sign. A house passing through an estate may need court papers before anyone can convey it, and the Indian River County clerk can tell you what has been filed. Keep utilities on and the yard tidy in the meantime.

Next, ask the building department about permits, call the tax collector for any balance, and gather keys and association papers. With those in hand, you can compare a listing against a cash offer using real numbers.

Once you accept an offer, the title company opens a file and searches the Indian River County records for mortgages, liens and judgments. Anything found is paid from your proceeds, so ask for payoff letters early. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which is where most conventional delays come from.

  1. Sign the contract and settle who pays title, stamp tax and recording.
  2. Close out or disclose any open permits.
  3. Sign the deed with the title agent or closing attorney.
  4. The clerk records the deed, and stamp tax is collected at that moment.
  5. The buyer files for their own homestead the following year.

If the house is vacant, hand over all keys and any gate or garage openers at closing, and cancel or transfer utilities that day.

sections.h2: Records a buyer's agent will want
sections.html:
Put together a short packet: the recorded deed, a recent tax bill, your permit list, and any association or utility account details. Add dated photos of past repairs and invoices for the roof, air conditioning and water heater.

  • Deed and any legal description or survey you have.
  • Permit numbers with final inspection dates.
  • Property tax bill and exemption status.
  • Repair invoices and warranty papers.

With this packet, you can answer a serious offer in a day, and cash buyers tend to return a price faster when the file is organized.

faqs.q: Does Sebastian have its own building department?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Sebastian Building Department is at 1225 Main St. and takes permits through the MGO portal or by email, with phone help at 772-589-5537. An owner-builder's first application must be made in person.

faqs.q: Will a buyer inherit my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The exemption follows the qualifying owner. After a sale the buyer files by March 1 for the following tax year, and the property is assessed at just value.

faqs.q: Who pays doc stamps on a Sebastian deed?
faqs.a: Both parties are liable under the statute, and your sale contract assigns the cost. At 70 cents per $100 of price, it is collected at the moment of recording.

faqs.q: Can I still sell in Sebastian when permits are open?
faqs.a: Yes, with disclosure. Ask the building department which permits are open and how a buyer's title company would treat them. Cash buyers often accept open permits at a lower price.

faqs.q: What is a typical home value in Sebastian?
faqs.a: The typical owner-estimated value is $317,000 (2020-2024). Those are owner estimates, so compare recent nearby sales before pricing.
